note: Golden vectors copied byte for byte from the N2 S1 contract. The Python generator refuses to run if either file's SHA-256 differs. They are the cross-language oracle: S1's TypeScript tests are the source, this package carries its own drift test and never the other way round.

notCopied.launcher-lines.json: L1 (daemon and launcher) NDJSON: not the worker's layer
notCopied.stop-receipts.json: Class A and B receipts are minted by the launcher: not the worker's layer

relayBlind.note: The contract says bootstrap and runtime payloads are relayed blind by the launcher and the worker. These mux negatives are refused by the TypeScript parser (daemon side) for their PAYLOAD and are therefore deliberately PASSED THROUGH by the worker, which checks headers only for those classes. The C test asserts exactly this.
